title: Road Rush
description: A road rush camera sits low to the asphalt, speed as smear, headlights and lane lines as weapons. The road is the subject; a vehicle is optional.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Intros to chases, night highways, a nightmare of driving: get down and let tarmac fill the frame. Lane dashes streak; light becomes paint.
A standing-height car commercial is not this shot. FPV is flight; this is tarmac.
Do not rise to a pretty three-quarter beauty pass unless you end there on purpose.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Low mount, bumper height or below, wide, shutter that allows streak. Lane lines, cat's eyes, wet asphalt.
Motion blur as paint. Prompt: Road-rush of [Subject], low to the asphalt, speed as smear, headlights and lane lines as weapons.

blocks.text: Tron Legacy's highway treats lanes as weapons of light. Death Proof keeps the camera down on asphalt as a threat.
Grammar: low, fast, tarmac as the subject.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a car commercial from standing height. The tell: you can read the whole vehicle cleanly and the asphalt is a thin strip.
The fix: drop to the tarmac, streak the lanes, let the road own the frame.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Road Rush in film?
Road rush is a low camera on asphalt at speed, with lane lines and headlights streaking. The road is the subject.
Road Rush vs Car Chasing
Car chasing covers pursuit from a second vehicle. Road rush can ignore the hunter and treat tarmac, lanes, and smear as the event.
When should I use Road Rush?
Use it for night highways, chase intros, and driving as threat. Do not use it as a standing-height product pass.
How do I prompt Road Rush for AI image or video?
Write a low rush along asphalt with streaking lanes. Example: Road-rush of [Subject], low to the asphalt, speed as smear, headlights and lane lines as weapons.
